purpose: Use PriorityTag only for the priority of a ticket, task or request on the urgent → low scale, or for "no priority"; the severity of a finding or alert is a SeverityTag, and the state of a ticket is a StatusIndicator or a Tag. PriorityTag labels a work item with how soon it should be handled: urgent, high, medium, low or none. The level reads from a three-bar signal glyph (the filled bars count the level), from a distinct alert mark for urgent, from three flat dots for none, and from the label, so no level depends on colour alone. Its accessible name always says the axis ("Priority: High"), which is why it is its own component and not a SeverityTag (decision SUP-05).
useWhen: Show how urgent a support ticket, task, issue or request is, in a ticket list row, a table cell, a board card or a ticket detail header.
Rank work on the fixed urgent, high, medium, low scale used by help desks and issue trackers, with "no priority" for items nobody has triaged yet.
avoidWhen: The value is how severe a finding, alert, incident or vulnerability is → use `severity-tag`.
The value is the state of the ticket (open, pending, solved) → use `status-indicator` or `tag`.
The user picks or changes the priority (a priority field or filter) → use `select` or `chip`; show the chosen value with this tag elsewhere.
The value is a count on an icon or avatar → use `badge`.
related: `severity-tag` — the same frame and bar glyph for the critical → info findings scale; its accessible name is the level alone.
`tag` — a toned status or category label with no order between values.
`status-indicator` — the live state of a resource or ticket.
`chip` — an interactive or removable token, for priority filters.
bestPractices: Keep the default label (the level name from the locale catalog, translated under `ConfigProvider`); override `label` only when the product glossary names a level differently (`Normal` for medium).
Show `none` for an untriaged item instead of leaving the cell empty, so the column reads the same on every row.
Use one PriorityTag per row, in its own column, so the glyphs line up and the scale reads down the column.
Do not add a toned `tag` beside it for the same level; the glyph and the label already carry it.
